law_enforcement_transparency.evidence: Falls under Amazon transparency reporting. Explicitly 'does not honor Do Not Track signals.' Combination with Amazon customer data expands scope of disclosable information.

content_moderation_equity.evidence: Generally LGBTQ+-friendly culture. Has specific LGBTQ+ tags and content categories. Drag and queer content thrives on platform. Community Guidelines explicitly protect gender identity and sexual orientation.

anti_harassment_protections.gap_note: Good on-platform tools (pronoun tags, AutoMod) but Amazon data combination means a harassment-related data breach exposes far more than just Twitch activity — purchase history, viewing habits, and Alexa data could all be linked.
anti_harassment_protections.evidence: Pronoun display tags and identity-based harassment detection are genuine strengths. But data combined with Amazon customer data means a breach or LE request exposes a much wider identity surface than Twitch activity alone. Channel-level moderation quality varies.

cross_border_safety.evidence: Amazon/US-based operations. Standard international data transfer practices. No specific high-risk jurisdiction concerns beyond standard global operations.

content_license_scope.gap_note: Claims 'We claim no ownership rights' but grants perpetual, irrevocable, transferable license with no deletion carve-out. All data can be 'DELETED, ALTERED, MOVED OR TRANSFERRED AT ANY TIME...WITH OR WITHOUT NOTICE.'
content_license_scope.evidence: Perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable, transferable, worldwide license in 'any form, media or technology, whether now known or hereafter developed.'

ai_ml_training.evidence: No mention of AI/ML. But perpetual irrevocable license covers 'any form, media or technology, whether now known or hereafter developed.' No opt-out.

content_removal_power.evidence: 'ANY DATA...MAY BE DELETED, ALTERED, MOVED OR TRANSFERRED AT ANY TIME FOR ANY REASON...WITH OR WITHOUT NOTICE AND WITH NO LIABILITY OF ANY KIND.'

post_deletion_survival.gap_note: 'Creator-friendly' positioning contradicts perpetual irrevocable license with no termination on deletion.
post_deletion_survival.evidence: Perpetual, irrevocable license with no termination-upon-deletion provision.

account_termination.evidence: 'Without notice and liability for any reason...or for no reason.' No refunds. Bound by terms even after termination. No appeal process.

dispute_resolution.evidence: Mandatory ICC arbitration in London. Class action waiver. 30-day opt-out. ICC arbitration can be prohibitively expensive.

terms_change_process.evidence: Updates last modified date, notifies of material changes. Continued use = acceptance. No advance notice period.

data_collection_breadth.evidence: Government IDs, tax IDs, all user content, stream metadata, analytics data, geolocation. Third-party data from social media, business partners, public sources.

third_party_sharing.evidence: Shares with Kick entities, ad networks, social media platforms. Permits third-party ad networks to collect data directly. No explicit 'we do not sell.'

tracking_advertising.evidence: Interest-based advertising. Shares hashed emails and AdIDs with social media platforms. Google Analytics and Facebook pixels. 'Not responsible for effectiveness' of opt-outs.

data_retention_deletion.evidence: No specific timelines. 'Legal hold' for threatened claims. ToS perpetual license undermines deletion rights.

readability_honesty.gap_note: Privacy Policy opens with 'creator-friendly streaming service' but ToS has most hostile terms analyzed. Largest gap between marketing and legal reality.
readability_honesty.evidence: 'Creator-friendly' marketing vs. no audit rights, 30-day payment disputes, all data deletable without notice, perpetual irrevocable license.

encryption_security.evidence: 'Reasonable precautions.' No specifics. Disclaims all security warranties.

creator_monetization.gap_note: Despite 'creator-friendly' branding, has most hostile creator terms: no audit rights, only Kick's records count, 30-day dispute window, payment withheld at discretion.
creator_monetization.evidence: 'No other measurements or statistics of any kind shall be accepted by Company...and you shall have no audit rights hereunder.' 30-day dispute window or claims waived forever.

sensitive_data_handling.evidence: Collects government IDs and tax IDs for monetization. Third-party data from social media, business partners, and public sources combined. Geolocation data collected.

real_name_requirements.evidence: Government ID required for monetization and identity verification. Username-based for viewers but streamers must provide legal identity documentation.

law_enforcement_transparency.evidence: No published transparency report. Minimal transparency about government data request handling. Australian company with Curacao operations — less established civil liberties framework than US-based peers.

content_moderation_equity.evidence: Less moderated overall — which means more freedom for LGBTQ+ expression but also less protection from anti-LGBTQ+ content. No specific LGBTQ+ content protections documented.

anti_harassment_protections.evidence: Minimal anti-harassment infrastructure. No specific identity-based harassment protections. Limited moderation tools compared to competitors. No pronoun tags or identity-affirming features.

cross_border_safety.evidence: Australian parent company with Curacao (Netherlands Antilles) operations. Data potentially processed across multiple jurisdictions. 'Not responsible for effectiveness' of third-party opt-outs suggests limited control over data flows.

content_license_scope.gap_note: Says 'Creators keep full ownership' and 'We will never try to steal your creations' directly alongside a perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable worldwide license.
content_license_scope.evidence: Perpetual, irrevocable, sublicensable, worldwide license covering 'all formats and channels now known or later developed.'

ai_ml_training.gap_note: No AI/ML mention but perpetual irrevocable license covers 'all formats and channels now known or later developed.' Non-binding reassurance doesn't override legal grant.
ai_ml_training.evidence: License covers 'all formats and channels now known or later developed.' Privacy Policy mentions 'generative AI services' as service provider category.

content_removal_power.evidence: Can cancel memberships and remove content 'at our sole discretion.' No explicit notice requirement.

post_deletion_survival.gap_note: 'Creators keep full ownership' yet license is perpetual irrevocable with no termination on deletion. 'These terms remain in effect even if you no longer have an account.'
post_deletion_survival.evidence: Perpetual, irrevocable license with no termination clause. Terms survive account closure.

account_termination.gap_note: Includes punitive clause: if you bring a claim against termination of another person, 'you are responsible for the damages caused, including attorneys' fees.'
account_termination.evidence: Terminate or suspend 'at any time at our sole discretion.' Punitive clause against challenging others' terminations.

dispute_resolution.evidence: No forced arbitration. No class action waiver. San Francisco courts. California law. Relatively straightforward.

terms_change_process.evidence: Will notify of material changes before they take effect. Materiality determined at Patreon's 'sole discretion.' Continued use = acceptance.

liability_indemnification.evidence: Broad indemnification with legal fees. Liability limited to 'amount of money we have earned through your use' — scales with earnings, better than flat $100 cap.

data_collection_breadth.evidence: Standard collection: name, email, phone, payment, IP, device info, social media profile data. No biometrics or GPS. Research studies may record video/audio (opt-in).

third_party_sharing.evidence: 'We never sell your information to third parties.' Creator Privacy Promise. Sharing limited to service providers, creators (necessary for membership), legal compliance.

tracking_advertising.evidence: Interest-based advertising with opt-out (DAA, iOS, Android). Does not honor DNT. Marketing opt-out available. Default-on tracking.

data_retention_deletion.evidence: Stores data 'until no longer necessary or until you ask us to delete it.' Privacy Center deletion mechanism. May retain for legal compliance.

readability_honesty.gap_note: Clearest gap in the dataset: 'We will never try to steal your creations' is legally non-binding within a binding perpetual irrevocable license.
readability_honesty.evidence: 'Creators keep full ownership' + 'We will never try to steal your creations' vs. perpetual irrevocable sublicensable worldwide license.

encryption_security.evidence: 'Industry standards' referenced but defers to separate Security Policy. No specifics. Payment tokenization used.

creator_monetization.evidence: Fee structure described (platform, processing, payout, currency conversion). Details in Help Center. Can withhold for violations. Legacy rates for founding creators.

sensitive_data_handling.evidence: Standard payment and creator data. No biometrics or GPS. Research studies may record video/audio but are opt-in. Privacy Policy does not list sensitive identity categories as collected data.

real_name_requirements.evidence: Real name required for payment processing and tax compliance. Creator names displayed publicly can be pen names but legal identity required on backend. Patrons use display names.

law_enforcement_transparency.evidence: Creator Privacy Promise limits data sharing. 'We never sell your information to third parties.' Standard legal compliance for government requests. US-based with established legal framework.

content_moderation_equity.gap_note: Generally LGBTQ+-friendly but payment processor pressure (Visa, Mastercard, PayPal) has forced removal of some LGBTQ+ adult content categories. Platform's ability to protect queer content is constrained by financial infrastructure.
content_moderation_equity.evidence: Allows adult content including LGBTQ+ adult content in principle. But payment processor policies have forced content restrictions that disproportionately affect LGBTQ+ adult creators. Platform caught between inclusive intent and payment infrastructure constraints.

anti_harassment_protections.evidence: Community Guidelines include anti-harassment provisions. Limited direct harassment vectors due to creator-patron model. But enforcement tools for creators against patron harassment are basic.

cross_border_safety.evidence: US-centric operations. Standard international data transfers. Creator-patron relationship model limits data exposure surface compared to social networks.

content_license_scope.evidence: Royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide license. Framed as for 'technical adaptation across devices.' Creators retain ownership.

ai_ml_training.gap_note: No explicit AI/ML mention in ToS but Privacy Policy reveals 'generative AI services' as a service provider category while content license is perpetual and irrevocable.
ai_ml_training.evidence: Privacy Policy lists 'generative AI services' as service providers. Perpetual irrevocable license. No opt-out mentioned.

content_removal_power.evidence: Can terminate accounts at discretion. Public posts may remain accessible elsewhere.

post_deletion_survival.evidence: Perpetual irrevocable license. Account deletion removes posts but 'public Posts may remain available elsewhere.'

account_termination.evidence: Can terminate at discretion. Minimal detail on grounds, notice, or appeal.

dispute_resolution.evidence: Mandatory JAMS arbitration in San Francisco. Class action waiver. No opt-out window mentioned.

terms_change_process.evidence: Changes communicated through site notices and emails. Continued use = acceptance. Legal notice emails binding even if opted out.

data_collection_breadth.evidence: Standard for publishing: name, email, phone, DOB, payment, social media info, DM contents. Hashed contacts for address book sync. No biometrics or GPS.

third_party_sharing.evidence: Shares with creators (name/email), service providers including 'generative AI services,' government authorities. No explicit 'we do not sell' in main policy.

tracking_advertising.evidence: Google Analytics, Facebook pixels, FullStory, Datadog. Does not honor DNT. Not heavily ad-focused (subscription model).

data_retention_deletion.evidence: Retains 'as long as reasonably necessary.' Deletion available through account settings. Public posts may persist.

readability_honesty.evidence: Structured and readable. Honestly notes DMs are not E2E encrypted. 'Generative AI services' disclosure easy to miss in service provider list.

encryption_security.evidence: DMs explicitly not E2E encrypted. Generic security language. Password-dependent account protection.

creator_monetization.evidence: Transparent model: creators set prices, keep majority minus Substack's well-known 10% cut. Details in separate Publisher Agreement.

sensitive_data_handling.evidence: Standard publisher data collection. No sensitive identity categories listed. Hashed contacts for address book sync. DM contents stored (not E2E encrypted) but platform is not identity-focused.

real_name_requirements.evidence: Allows pen names and pseudonymous publishing. Writers can maintain full anonymity from readers. Backend payment requires real identity but not displayed publicly.

law_enforcement_transparency.evidence: Limited transparency reporting. Privacy Policy lists 'generative AI services' as service providers which adds data-sharing surface. Standard legal compliance.

content_moderation_equity.gap_note: Minimal content moderation approach has been criticized for allowing anti-LGBTQ+ newsletters and content to thrive on platform without intervention.
content_moderation_equity.evidence: Very light-touch moderation policy. No documented LGBTQ+-specific content protections. Has hosted newsletters promoting anti-LGBTQ+ views. Platform design gives equal legitimacy to all publishers.

anti_harassment_protections.evidence: Limited anti-harassment tools. DMs are not E2E encrypted. Comment sections on posts have basic moderation. Newsletter model limits but doesn't eliminate harassment vectors.

cross_border_safety.evidence: US-centric operations. Standard data handling. Publishing model means content is public by design but personal data exposure is limited.

content_license_scope.evidence: Standard broad license. No perpetual/irrevocable language. Users retain ownership. Content from larger spaces used for safety features with user controls.

ai_ml_training.evidence: Transparent: uses content from 'larger spaces' for safety features. Users have privacy settings to control this. Not used from DMs. Safety-focused framing.

content_removal_power.evidence: Removes for policy or law violations. Users can edit/delete own content. Reports system. Automated detection for prohibited content.

post_deletion_survival.evidence: Full delete permanently removes identifying info. Anonymizes other data. Legal obligations may require retention.

account_termination.evidence: Termination for prohibited conduct. Disable (reactivate later) or full delete options. Trust and Safety team.

dispute_resolution.evidence: Mandatory arbitration for US/Canadian residents with class action waiver. But meaningful 30-day opt-out with clear email address.

terms_change_process.evidence: Prominent notice for significant changes via email or in-service. Publication dates always indicated.

liability_indemnification.evidence: $100 floor with 3-month lookback (shorter than 12-month standard). Low effective cap.

data_collection_breadth.evidence: Standard: username, email, messages, payment info, device info. Notably does NOT store voice/video call contents. Advance notice if this changes.

third_party_sharing.evidence: 'Doesn't sell personal information.' Subscription-based, not ad-driven. Shares with vendors, legal compliance, business transitions. Less ad-partner sharing.

tracking_advertising.evidence: Subscription-based revenue. Sponsored content (Quests) with user controls. Users can limit personalization and sponsored content. Less aggressive than ad-driven platforms.

data_retention_deletion.evidence: Retained until no longer needed. Both disable and full delete options. Data export within 30 days in JSON format.

readability_honesty.evidence: Transparent about business model. Honest about data practices. Key principles up front. Most transparent of all platforms analyzed.

encryption_security.evidence: E2E encryption for voice/video. Encryption at rest using TLS. All info encrypted in transit. 2FA available. Best security commitments of any platform.

creator_monetization.evidence: N/A - not a creator monetization platform.

sensitive_data_handling.gap_note: Positioned as privacy-respecting but text messages — where most sensitive identity conversations happen — are stored without E2E encryption. Phone number verification increasingly required. Age verification expanding data collection.
sensitive_data_handling.evidence: Text messages stored server-side without E2E encryption. Phone number verification increasingly pushed. Government ID uploads now required for age-gated content/servers. Voice/video is E2E encrypted but text is not.

real_name_requirements.gap_note: Was username-only but now requires government ID verification for age-gated servers and features. This forces queer users in age-restricted LGBTQ+ spaces to upload identity documents — directly contradicting Discord's pseudonymous reputation.
real_name_requirements.evidence: Government ID verification now required for age-gated servers and features. ID verification rollout expanding. Previously username-based with no real name requirement, but age verification mandate now links government identity to accounts accessing LGBTQ+ spaces that are age-restricted.

law_enforcement_transparency.gap_note: E2E encryption only covers voice/video — all text messages, DMs, and server conversations are stored unencrypted and fully disclosable to law enforcement. This is where most sensitive identity conversations happen.
law_enforcement_transparency.evidence: Publishes transparency report. But text messages, DMs, and server conversations are NOT E2E encrypted and are fully accessible via legal process. Only voice/video calls have E2E encryption. Government ID data from age verification is also disclosable.

content_moderation_equity.gap_note: Generally LGBTQ+-inclusive but age-gating requirements can disproportionately affect LGBTQ+ servers and content. Servers discussing sexuality/gender topics may be age-gated, requiring ID verification to access.
content_moderation_equity.evidence: LGBTQ+-inclusive community guidelines and anti-discrimination policies. But age-gating system can force LGBTQ+ servers into restricted categories. Server-based self-governance is a strength but also means protection depends on individual server moderators.

anti_harassment_protections.gap_note: Good moderation tools exist but government ID verification creates a new outing vector — if Discord's systems are breached, ID-verified users in LGBTQ+ servers are now linked to government identity.
anti_harassment_protections.evidence: Pronoun display, AutoMod, and identity-based harassment detection are genuine strengths. But ID verification requirement means a data breach now links government identity to server membership including LGBTQ+ servers. Server-level enforcement quality varies.

cross_border_safety.gap_note: E2E encryption claim is misleading for queer safety — only voice/video is E2E encrypted. All text conversations are stored server-side and accessible across jurisdictions.
cross_border_safety.evidence: Text messages, DMs, and server history are NOT E2E encrypted and are stored on Discord's servers. Global operations mean this data is accessible across jurisdictions. Voice/video E2E is good but doesn't protect the conversations where identity disclosure is most likely.
